lawyer:
M Golam Rabbani with AKM Asaduzzaman, Advocates ----- For the Appellants.  
AY Salehuzzaman, DAG  ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Noor Mohammad Khan & ors ----- Appellants  
Vs. 
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh & ors ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 10. We are to consider here whether the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title to the suit land. Ext. 1 is the receipt for payment of salami to the Dhaka Nowab Court of Wards Estate. Ext. 2 is the alleged Amalnama granted by the said Estate settling the suit land to the plaintiff No. 1 and Ext 3 series are the rent receipts granted for the years 1353, 1354 and 1358 B.S. by the said Estate. The appellants have not included the said documents in the Paper Book though the Rules provide that part II of the Paper Book shall consist of exhibits and no finding or conclusion in the decision appealed from will be permitted to be challenged at the hearing of the appeal unless the materials on which such challenge is based is included in the Paper Book. As such we are not bound to consider the said documents. However, we have perused the said documents in the lower court records. The contents of Exts. 1 and 3 series were written with pencil and Ext. 2 with ink as pointed out by the learned Deputy Attorney-General. He also pointed out that the receipts were rubbed to make the same appear old and the same were written with pencil instead of ink so as to avoid the same from being checked. We have noticed from Ext. 1 that the amount of salami was received subject to the approval of the Chief Manager and from the remarks in the bottom of the said Ext No. 1 it appears that salami and rents received without approval of the Chief Manager will not have the effect of settling the land of the Estate to the person paying the same. We find from Ext. 2 that it is a form of proposal for settlement of the land of the said Estate and there was no approval of the Chief Manager. We have also noticed from Ext. 3 series, rent receipts that unless settlement is approved by the authorised officer of the Estate claim or settlement of land cannot be made on the basis of payment of rent. In Ext. 2 it has also been clearly written that the proposal for settlement of land will not be effective unless the tenant executes kabuliyat in favour of the landlord. The plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1 stated that the receipt for payment of salami was signed by Gobinda Chandra Roy, Cashier of Dhaka Nowab Estate in his presence and the said receipt was marked Ext. 1. The said witness further stated in his deposition that the suit land was leased out to him by the document of lease executed by the officers of Nowab Estate including Assistant Manager, Dhaka Nowab Estate by signing before him and the document was marked Ext. 2. He further stated that these are the signatures of the Head Assistant and Assistant Manager in the said document marked Exts. 2(i) and 2(ii). He further stated that he paid rent to the Nowab Estate afterwards and rent receipts were granted by the Dhaka Nowab Estate and the same were marked Ext. 3 series. From the cross-examination of this witness we find that he was a school student at the relevant time of taking lease and that he did not pay any rent from 1359 BS upto date. PW 5, who claimed himself to be an ex-employee of Dhaka Nowab Court of Wards Estate as orderly of the then Assistant Manager, stated in his deposition that the Assistant Manager Abul Kashem executed Ext. 2 in his presence and proved his signature marked Ext. 2(ii). He further stated that receipt of salami Ext.1 and rent receipts were granted by Dhaka Nowab Estate. From his cross-examination, we find that he is an illiterate person and he could not satisfy the court that he ever worked as orderly of the said Estate. We are unable to place any reliance on the testimony of PW 5. He appears to be a procured witness who does not know how to sign his name and put his thumb impression in the deposition sheet. PW1 being the plaintiff and a school student at the relevant time on his own admission cannot also be relied on as he is interested in the result of the suit. The contents of the said documents were not even attempted to be proved by the PW1. Considering the evidence of the said witnesses we arc of the view that the said documents were not legally proved as writing of the said documents could not be proved by examining any witness. We are unable to appreciate the argument of the learned Advocate of the appellants that the said documents were legally proved. The decision referred to by the learned Advocate has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. From the very look the said documents appear to be spurious and manufactured for the purpose of the suit in collusion with the interested persons. Even if these documents are accepted as genuine the same could not create title in favour of the plaintiffs in the absence of the approval by the Chief Manager and execution of kabuliyat in compliance thereof. It appears that the alleged settlement by the said document were not acted upon as the plaintiffs failed to produce any rent receipts granted by the Government after the acquisition of rent receiving interest nor they could produce any khatian alleged to be prepared in the name of their alleged tenants in respect of part of the suit plot or any compensation assessment roll in the name of the plaintiffs or in respect of the said tenanted land or any khatian alleged to have been prepared in the name of the plaintiff No. 1 at the initial stage. Moreover, the PW 1 himself admitted that he did not pay rent from 1359 BS upto date.
